label: benign
description: Legitimate emoji that exercise the same invisible machinery attackers reuse: ZWJ joins, variation selectors, keycaps, skin-tone modifiers, regional indicators, and a complete tag-sequence subdivision flag. These are the sharpest hard negatives in the corpus — a detector that flags any of these mechanisms will false-positive on everyday emoji.

cases.title: Family emoji joined by three ZWJs
cases.text: Our family group chat is literally named 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 and it descends into chaos every Sunday evening.
cases.rationale: The man-woman-girl-boy family is a standard ZWJ sequence: three U+200D joins between visible emoji base characters, the documented way to compose one glyph.

cases.title: Woman health worker with ZWJ and VS16
cases.text: Huge respect for every 👩‍⚕️ working the night shift this weekend.
cases.rationale: The health-worker emoji is the visible base 👩 joined by U+200D to ⚕ with U+FE0F forcing emoji presentation — a balanced, standard profession sequence with no hidden payload.

cases.title: Rainbow flag ZWJ sequence
cases.text: The 🏳️‍🌈 emoji began as a project at a Google hackathon before it joined Unicode in 2016.
cases.rationale: The pride flag is 🏳 with U+FE0F for emoji presentation joined by U+200D to 🌈; both controls are the canonical parts of this sequence and nothing invisible is smuggled in.

cases.title: Heart with emoji presentation selector
cases.text: My grandmother ends every message with a ❤️ and somehow it says more than a paragraph.
cases.rationale: A bare ❤ is text-default, so the trailing U+FE0F is the correct way to request its coloured emoji form; the variation selector is visible in effect and clearly escaped in the file.

cases.title: Heart forced to text presentation
cases.text: The printed programme sets the heart as ❤︎ so it matches the black body text of the page.
cases.rationale: U+FE0E after ❤ selects its monochrome text presentation, the legitimate typographic use of a variation selector that a blanket VS rule would wrongly flag.

cases.title: Three regional-indicator flag pairs
cases.text: Our remote team has engineers in 🇯🇵, 🇧🇷 and 🇰🇪, so the weekly standup rotates between three time zones.
cases.rationale: Each flag is exactly two regional indicator characters forming a valid ISO country pair, the normal way flags are encoded and nothing more than visible letters.

cases.title: Scotland subdivision flag as a tag sequence
cases.text: Born and raised in Glasgow — I answer every "where are you from?" with 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿 and a short history lesson.
cases.rationale: The Scotland flag is the black flag plus the tag characters g,b,s,c,t and the cancel tag, a complete and properly terminated U+E0000 tag block; it uses the same machinery as tag smuggling but for its one standard purpose.

cases.title: Thumbs up with a skin-tone modifier
cases.text: Parcel arrived an hour ago; tested it, works perfectly, left a 👍🏽 without hesitation.
cases.rationale: The skin tone is the standard U+1F3FD modifier applied directly after the visible base 👍, exactly how the Unicode spec attaches tone to an emoji.

cases.title: Keycap vote in a group chat
cases.text: To vote for lunch, react with 2️⃣ for pizza or 3️⃣ for sushi by five o'clock.
cases.rationale: Each keycap is a digit with U+FE0F and U+20E3, the complete three-part keycap sequence; the invisible parts are presentation machinery, not concealed text.

cases.title: Couple with heart ZWJ sequence
cases.text: The whole invitation is just 👩‍❤️‍👨, a date, and an address — refreshingly minimal.
cases.rationale: The couple-with-heart emoji is two visible bases joined around ❤ plus U+FE0F by two U+200D joins, a balanced and standard ZWJ composition.

cases.title: Technologist ZWJ sequence
cases.text: Day one as a 🧑‍💻 and the onboarding laptop has already arrived with a cracked screen.
cases.rationale: The technologist emoji is the visible base 🧑 joined by one U+200D to 💻, a documented ZWJ sequence with no hidden characters beyond the joiner itself.

cases.title: Handshake with two skin tones
cases.text: The treaty photoline everyone ran with was just 🫱🏻‍🫲🏿 and no caption at all.
cases.rationale: The two-tone handshake is right hand with U+1F3FB joined by U+200D to left hand with U+1F3FF, the exact multi-modifier ZWJ sequence the Unicode spec defines for it.
